description: Octal 16-bit DAC SPI, internal reference
notes: GRADE LOCKED TO C. The grade letter selects REFERENCE GAIN as well as reset state - A/B are gain 1 (2.500V full scale), C/D are gain 2 (5.000V). An A-grade part would halve everything: pitch -2…+2.25V, mods +-5V, and channel 7 could not reach 2.500V at all. This row previously read 'DAC8568C (or A grade)' and explained the letter as reset state only. C also clears to ZERO scale where B/D clear to midscale and would park pitch octaves up. Populate 6 of 8: pitch, 4 mods, mod offset; channels 6 and 8 spare. Internal ref DISABLED by default, enable at boot. GAIN/GRADE MAPPING CONFIRMED 2026-09-21 against SBAS430E, now in the repo at datasheets/analog/DAC8568CIPW.pdf and verified verbatim: 'For device grades A and C on power-up, all DAC registers are filled with zeros and the output voltages of all DAC channels are set to zero scale.' A/B = 2.5V FSR, C/D = 5V FSR. *** TWO RIDERS THE REPO DID NOT HAVE. *** (1) THE C GRADE REQUIRES AVDD 5.0V TO 5.5V - the Electrical Characteristics table specifies grades C/D only over that range, where A/B are specified 2.7-5.5V. The LM317 nominal is 5.21V so this passes, but E7 SELECTS R-REG-SET ON THE BENCH over a 0.66V worst-case spread: a selection that lands below 5.00V puts the DAC out of spec. 5.00V is now a HARD FLOOR on that bench step, which it was not before. (2) EXTERNAL VREFIN MUST BE <= AVDD/2 ON C/D, against <= AVDD on A/B. Not binding today because the internal reference is used, but it forecloses an external-reference retrofit at anything above ~2.6V. Also from SBAS430E: reference tempco is GRADE-DEPENDENT - C/D are 2 typ / 5 max ppm/degC where A/B are 5 typ / 25 max, so the 5 ppm/degC in the pitch error budget is the C-grade MAX and is the right number. Static reference mode auto-powers the reference with the DACs; Flexible mode (DB19=1) keeps it up regardless, and BOTH default to reference OFF after any power cycle

notes: Sensor reaches 4.7V into a 3V3 ADC. Divide AFTER the buffer, not before. >=10k upper leg: 5V-before-3V3 sequencing otherwise pushes ~2.5mA into the ADC ESD clamp on every power-up. Needs C-AA-ADC to still settle

description: Bulk at each WS2815 feed point
notes: Bulk belongs at the load. A ferrite is a wire at the WS2815's ~2kHz PWM rate

description: LC between the umbilical node and the buck input
notes: A real inductor, not a bead. This is the part the bead was wrongly credited for

description: SPI idle-state pulls at the module
notes: SIX, not three - BOTH SIDES of the 74AHCT125. Cable side: CS to +5V, SCLK and MOSI to ground, so the buffer's inputs do not float and crowbar when the instrument is absent. DAC side: same, because with OE disabled the buffer outputs are Hi-Z and it is then the DAC's SCLK/DIN/SYNC that float - which is the state these were bought for and the three cable-side pulls do not reach. Module-alive-instrument-off is the normal state, not a fault; a stray CS edge latches garbage into the pitch DAC. CABLE-SIDE CS PULLS TO 3V3, NOT +5V: pulled to 5V it drives 430uA continuously through the unpowered ESP32's input clamp in the design's NORMAL resting state, and the node sits at ~0.7V so 'CS idle high' is not even achieved. DAC-SIDE CS PULLS TO AVDD (the LM317's 5.21V), not bus +5V - a pull-up belongs on its consumer's rail, and on the bus rail a reversed ribbon reaches the DAC's SYNC pin and turns a $0.30 buffer failure into a DAC failure

description: Series termination on SCLK, MOSI and CS at the driving end
notes: THREE. 100R, not 220R - revised 2026-09-21. 2m of Cat5 is a 100-ohm TRANSMISSION LINE (20ns round trip against 2-5ns edges), not an RC corner, and three reviewers agreed the old RC derivation was the wrong model. At 220R the far end's first step is 1.83-1.86V against the 74AHCT125's 2.0V VIH, dwelling ~20ns per edge in the forbidden band on a part with no hysteresis. 100R gives a clean 2.75V single step and 33mA of fault current; 68R is electrically ideal but draws 48mA against a 40mA pad spec. carrier.md used to draw these as R-SCLK-SER / R-MOSI-SER / R-CS-SER, which were in no BOM

description: Series resistor on each op-amp + input driven by the DAC
notes: SEVEN. Now correct on the mod channels as well, because the two-resistor form drives the op-amp's (+) input directly - a true high-Z node where 1k causes no error. It was wrong on the OLD four-resistor version, where the 10k input resistor WAS the gain network and 1k in series unbalanced it. Pitch, mod 1-4, the mod offset buffer, the VREFOUT follower. DAC on 5.21V and op-amps on +-12V do not come up together; bounds clamp current, outside the feedback path so no accuracy cost

description: Clamp diodes on the DRIVER side of R-OUT-PROT
notes: MOVED to the op-amp side of the 1k, which fixes two things at once. (a) BACK-POWERING: clamped at the JACK, a neighbouring module driving 10V through its own 220R output pushes 42mA per jack into our +12V rail when this module is off - 254mA across six jacks, into the rail that also feeds the umbilical. Behind the 1k it is 7.6mA per jack. (b) LEAKAGE: inside the feedback loop the op-amp absorbs it, so the 2.4-cent BAT54S error goes to identically zero for any diode. BAV99 kept anyway - silicon costs nothing and the reasoning no longer depends on it. NOTE: no surveyed design clamps a CV output to the RAILS at all; every clamp in the corpus goes to GND. Erica Synths is the one that puts its clamp on the driver side, which is where this now is. SIX - one per OUTPUT jack including breath, whose schematic omitted it. The two BREATH INPUT clamps are a separate row, D-CLAMP-BREATH, so the module carries eight BAV99 in total

description: Helmholtz restrictor AND liquid-water barrier at the sensor port
notes: One part, two jobs: sizes the resonance above the 500Hz corner and blocks liquid. Size the orifice at E2. Trap volume <=1mL. Pressure port only - the DP's reference port is unplumbed

description: Conformal coating for the in-body boards
notes: Breathed into for hours behind 18 unsealed switch cutouts, interior 10-20K above ambient. MASK BOTH SENSOR PORTS FIRST - a sealed reference chamber gains ~5.2kPa when warm and the output clips at zero, looking like a dead sensor (ADR 0003)

description: Bonds the aluminium plate to PWR_GND
notes: PWR_GND, never AGND. Unbonded, the plate floats 1-2mm from 18 switch pins and fires spurious notes on touch. AGND would put body capacitance on the breath reference

description: Tail window for the 8x8 matrix
notes: NOT the side panels' frosted material - needs pixel definition, not blur. Thin and close to the LEDs. Prototype at M6

description: Umbilical cable, module to instrument
notes: STRANDED not solid-core: solid core work-hardens and fractures under constant flexing, which is this cable's whole life. Shielded preferred. It is a CONSUMABLE - keep spares and replace at the first intermittency

description: Mouthpiece - no bite sensor, raw tube is playable
notes: OD must let the lips vent at the corners - that is what makes circular breathing work. Bore settled at E2 by playing two or three sizes. Removable for cleaning

description: INA828 gain-set resistor
notes: G = 1 + 50k/42.2k = 2.185. Effective 2.161 after the bias/series divider -> 9.94V jack span. The panel gain knob absorbs the 0.6%

description: Common-mode bias return, one per in-amp input
notes: REPLACES R-PD-BREATH. Without these the in-amp floats when unplugged and saturates to a rail. ~60nA against a 350mA power return = 0.2ppm, so AGND's no-current rule survives

description: Module-side series protection, one per leg
notes: Matched. Gigaohm in-amp inputs make source impedance irrelevant to CMRR, so 10k is free

description: 500Hz filter AHEAD of the in-amp
notes: 482Hz differential (NOT 531Hz - that assumed 20k of series resistance; adding R1b to the return leg makes both legs 11k). C_diff must be ~10x C_cm or a CM mismatch converts to DM. AHEAD of the amp, not after - a filter after it cannot stop RF rectification from a 2.4GHz radio 2m away

description: Breath output reconstruction cap
notes: ~480Hz with R-OUT-PROT. Film not X7R: DC bias coefficient moves the corner 30% at 10V. ON THE JACK SIDE of R-OUT-PROT, never the op-amp side - inside the loop it is a capacitive load and the stage can oscillate.

description: Sets the load switch current limit
notes: THE resistor that is the limit. 1.0A target. The stated 0.9-1.13A window is +-11% and is NARROWER THAN THE LT1641'S OWN SENSE-THRESHOLD TOLERANCE - the same mistake already found and fixed on the LM317 divider, one row down. So E6 measures the TRIP as well as the load, with a current probe, and the value is selected on the bench like R-REG-SET | 2026-09-21, from the banked 164112fc.pdf p.2: V_SENSETRIP is specified 39 / 47 / 55 mV (min/typ/max) at VFB=1V, i.e. +-17%. So R-ILIM at 50mohm gives a limit of 0.78 / 0.94 / 1.10 A. THE ROW'S OWN OBJECTION IS CONFIRMED BY THE DATASHEET: a +-11% window IS narrower than the part's own sense-threshold tolerance. E6 measures the trip with a current probe and selects the value. The foldback floor at VFB=0 is 8/12/17mV, i.e. 160/240/340 mA - the low corner is what a hot-plug has to climb out of, and the worked start in power-entry.md uses the 12mV typ

description: Series protection on the breath buffer output into the umbilical
notes: TWO, not one, and 1206 not 0805 - both changed with the schematic and this row did not follow. R1 in the BREATH leg, R1b its twin in the AGND leg: the return leg carries no signal current, so a matching resistor costs no differential gain and is what keeps the 1M bias pair from capping CMRR at 60dB on its own. 1206 because ADR 0003's designed-safe sustained +12V fault puts 11.8mA through R1: 139mW against an 0805's ~125mW. Both are instrument-side and UNRETROFITTABLE

description: Reconstruction filter cap on mod 1-4 outputs
notes: 1k x 82nF = 1.94kHz. Real attenuation on the 3.6kHz ZOH image that a 15.9kHz corner ignores. FOUR not five: breath does not pass through the DAC and has its own 330nF (C-OUT-BREATH, ~480Hz). ON THE JACK SIDE of R-OUT-PROT, never the op-amp side - inside the loop it is a capacitive load and the stage can oscillate. PACKAGE IS PROBABLY WRONG: 82nF in C0G/NP0 almost certainly does not exist in 0805 - C0G permittivity puts that value in 1210 or larger. Unverified because every distributor site was proxy-blocked. Options if it is not buyable: 1210, a film part, or raise the corner and take less attenuation on the 4kHz image

description: Two-resistor non-inverting network per mod channel
notes: EIGHT, not sixteen: R1=10k, R2=30k per channel, k=3 so gain = 1+k = 4 exactly and the intercept is k x V_ref with V_ref = 3.3333V from the offset channel. Lands on EXACTLY +-10.000V, where the old four-resistor difference amp needed a 40.2k fudge to reach +-10.05. One matching requirement per channel instead of two, and the CLR-safe property survives because both terms still go to zero. Buy from one reel. See hardware/module/mod-channels/mod-channels.md

notes: DECIDED 2026-09-21: J-CHAIN is a 2x6 IDC on a 12-way ribbon, alternating ground - GND SCK GND SH/LD GND SER GND QH GND 3V3 spare spare. This replaces the tail-mounted alternative's 32-44 conductors and ~46 hand-terminated joints

description: Bulk cap at the umbilical entry / buck input - the C of L-BUCK-IN's LC
notes: Completes the LC: L-BUCK-IN had an L and no C. One per buck. Also the capacitance the module load switch's inrush ramp is sized against (ADR 0005). 25V part on a 12V rail for derating

description: HF decoupling at every carrier IC - ADC, reference, buffer, level shifter, sensor
notes: One per supply pin: MCP3202, REF5050 IN AND OUT, OPA2197 +12V, 74AHCT125, MPXV4006DP, and both R-78E5 inputs. ADR 0001 fixed only the shift registers (C-DECOUPLE-165) and stopped there | 2026-09-21: QTY 7 -> 8. The old enumeration gave the REF5050 one 100nF while carrier.md drew one at its OUTPUT and the prose claimed one at the sensor's VS pin - the same part spent twice across three files, and none drawn at VS at all. SBOS410O section 9.4.1.1 pp.29-30 wants both: a VIN bypass AND 'a high-frequency, 1uF capacitor in parallel between the output and ground'. Settled allocation is REF5050 VIN, REF5050 VOUT, and SKT-BREATH VS - and the VS one is the 100 nF the reference buffer's compensation is designed against. See figures.yaml cref-out-node

description: Output and input capacitors on the REF5050
notes: REF5050 VIN bypass and REF5050 VOUT load capacitor - one each, with a 100nF from C-DECOUPLE-CARRIER alongside each. NEITHER IS ON THE BUFFER'S OUTPUT. This is the rail that IS the breath scale factor | 2026-09-21, from the banked SBOS410O. *** THE NODE IS SETTLED: see figures.yaml cref-out-node. *** The part is forced onto the REF5050's own VOUT because the part cannot be built without it - section 8.4.1 p.26 verbatim: 'Confirm that a output capacitor (CL) is connected from VOUT to GND. For output stability, verify that the ESR value of CL less than or equal to 1.5 ohm.' Figure 8-6: CL = 1uF to 50uF for REF50xxI, REF50xxAI. So one of the two is not a choice, and the other is the section 8.4.1 supply bypass (1-10uF) - which accounts for both and leaves nothing for the buffer output. Independently, 10uF there would be 10000x the OPA2197's specified 1 nF capacitive-load limit (SBOS737C p.1 and section 7.3.5 p.22). CONSEQUENCE WORTH WRITING DOWN: the REF5050 now drives only the OPA2197's input bias current (+-20 pA max at 25 C), so its load regulation - 20 ppm/mA typ, 30 max, 50 over temperature, p.7 - contributes ZERO to the breath scale factor, where the other topology would have cost 300 ppm = 1.0 LSB | THE 'MISSING SERIES 1-1.5 OHM RESISTOR' CLAIMED HERE EARLIER IS WITHDRAWN. That read an upper bound as a requirement: section 8.4.1's 'ESR less than or equal to 1.5 ohm' is the STABILITY ceiling, which an X7R satisfies trivially; the 1-1.5 ohm window is a separate NOISE recommendation, and section 9.4.1.1 p.29 says plainly 'A resistor in series with the output capacitor is optional.' Arithmetic: the REF5050's own 10 Hz-1 kHz noise is 0.9 uVrms/V = 4.5 uVrms on 5.000 V, against one ADC LSB at VS of 1.46 mV - a margin of 325x. Gain-peaking on a term 325x below an LSB is not a defect. FIT A 0R/1R0 FOOTPRINT in series with the VOUT capacitor and decide it at E13 with a scope; it is electrically free either way, being in series with a capacitor to ground rather than in the signal path. The TRIM/NR 1uF is DECLINED for the same reason: section 8.3.6 p.26 halves 4.5 uVrms to 2.25 uVrms and lengthens start-up, on a term already 325x below an LSB

description: Entry bulk capacitance downstream of each bead
notes: NOT 47uF on every rail. The +12V branch carries the LM317's divider, the DAC and the comparator, about 22mA against -12V's 10mA - so at 47uF each it collapses 2.2x faster and every rack power-down leaves the op-amps with V+ near 0 and V- at -6 to -8V for ~30ms, pulling all six jacks toward the surviving negative rail. 100uF on +12V balances the decay. 10-100uF per rail per ADR 0004; NOT the strip capacitance, which belongs at the load and is C-STRIP-BULK

description: Socket for the MPXV4006DP so the sensor is replaceable
notes: ADR 0003 calls the sensor a wear part and buys two. The spare is only reachable if the first part comes out. The body opens on six fasteners now (ADR 0009), so replacing the sensor is a bench job rather than impossible - but it is still behind the lid, which is why it is socketed. Case 1351-01 THT leads on 2.54mm

description: Panel power indicator
notes: A PLAIN POWER LED off the module's own rail, like every other Eurorack module's. It used to be driven by a presence comparator that watched the breath line - that comparator is DELETED, and with it the only thing in the module that tried to know whether the instrument was there. Health reporting belongs in the instrument, which has a display, a web app and the actual data. With LT1641-1 latching off on a fault, this still says why the instrument went dark

description: Series resistor for LED-PANEL
notes: ~4mA from the module's +12V analog rail. Was 820R from bus +5V when it shared a node with the level shifter's OE pins; that node is gone with the comparator

description: Breath response: log (CCW) - linear (centre) - exponential (CW)
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-21. Same part as POT-GAIN. The centre detent is honestly warranted here and not elsewhere: at centre the wiper sits at exactly 0V by topology (it spans +Vin/2 and -Vin/2), so the nonlinear branch carries no current and the stage is mathematically linear - unlike POT-OFFSET, whose detent review found lands ~20deg off its true zero | 2026-09-21, from the genuine Taiwan Alpha RV09 series datasheet now in the repo (datasheets/connectors/RV09AF-40.pdf). FOUR THINGS THE ORDER CODE HAS TO CARRY, none of which this row said. (1) THE PLAIN -40 HAS NO BUSHING AT ALL - it is snap-in, and the panel needs only shaft clearance. A bushing is a SUFFIX: E1 = metal M9x0.75, E1N = plastic D9, and either makes the panel hole ~9.5mm instead of a shaft hole. (2) CENTRE DETENT IS SUFFIX 0C, and it costs half the life: 5000 rotations with the click against 10000 without. (3) THE A/B LETTER IN RV09A / RV09B IS THE ROTATIONAL ANGLE (280 +/-5 deg vs 300 +/-5 deg), NOT THE TAPER. The taper is a separate A/B/C code. This is a standing trap and the row said nothing about it. (4) Body 9.8mm wide, 11.4mm across the snap-in lugs, 7.0mm board-to-shaft for every -40, shaft D6.0 0/-0.1. THREE ACROSS 50.50mm IS 34.2mm - the pot body is nowhere near binding and the 14mm knob is the constraint, which settles the open question this row carried. NOTE THE PART MAY NOT BE ALPHA: Thonk ships the Song Huei R0904N, dimensionally interchangeable (datasheets/connectors/R0904N.pdf)

description: Sets response curve strength
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-21. First sizing, targeting ~1.5x gain ratio at a hard blow (4.64V at the in-amp). This is the knob that decides how strong 'fully exponential' feels and wants a bench pass with a player, not a spreadsheet

description: Nonlinear element for the response shaper
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-21. Breath is unipolar so only one ever conducts in play; the second covers the power-on and fault excursions the 2026-09-21 review catalogued. Scaling is set at /2 so the 0.6V knee lands at about a quarter of a hard blow - at /10 it would sit ABOVE the playing range and the control would do nothing until you overblow, which was caught by checking and not by inspection | 2026-09-21: TWO 1N4148W datasheets banked. Vishay Document Number 86356 Rev 1.0 16-Nov-2023 (NOT 85748, which is a genuine 404) at datasheets/discrete-and-power/1N4148W.pdf, true SOD-123: 2.7 x 1.55mm body, 3.7mm overall, 1.175mm high, R-thJA 440 K/W, P_tot 280mW on the recommended footprint, I_F(AV) 250mA, V_F <=1V at 10mA, C_D 1.5pF max, t_rr 4ns. Diotec's 1N4148W at 1N4148W-DIOTEC.pdf is *** SOD-123F, NOT SOD-123 *** - flat lead, no standoff - so this row's 'SOD-123 or SOD-323' has to name the manufacturer. Use Vishay's 440 K/W / 280mW as the conservative thermal pair; Diotec's 312 K/W / 400mW assume 3mm2 of copper per terminal. *** THE '0.6 V KNEE' THIS ROW'S SHAPER DEPENDS ON IS NOT-IN-DOCUMENT AS A SPEC. *** Neither datasheet specifies V_F at 0.6V; it is readable only off Vishay's TYPICAL Fig.1 (~1mA at 25degC) and that curve shifts more than 100mV left at 150degC. For a shaper whose entire behaviour is where the knee sits, that temperature shift was unrecorded here. The tightest SPECIFIED bound in the bank is Diotec's V_F < 0.855V at 10mA, still 250mV above the asserted knee

description: Response shaper: 1/2 shapes at /2 inverting, 1/2 restores x2 inverting
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-21. This stage consumes BOTH remaining spare OPA2197 halves, so the separate A5 finding - POT-OFFSET's wiper is unbuffered, which is why its zero sits ~20deg past centre at +0.605V - needs this additional package. Both are review findings, so the package is not spare capacity being spent on a whim | 2026-09-21: SBOS737C is banked at datasheets/analog/OPA2197.pdf, 56pp. TWO CORRECTIONS THAT MATTER. (1) *** OPEN-LOOP OUTPUT IMPEDANCE IS SPECIFIED AND IT IS 375 OHM, NOT THE 75.8 OHM THIS CORPUS BACK-SOLVED. *** EC table p.8 and p.10: 'ZO Open-loop output impedance | f = 1 MHz, IO = 0 A, See Figure 26 | 375 | ohm'. Figure 26 reads ~3.26k at 0.1Hz, 482 at 10Hz, a 375 plateau from 100Hz to 300kHz, 301 at 1MHz and ~73 at 10MHz - so 75.8 ohm is roughly the 10MHz value, i.e. a defensible HF number, but it is NOT TI's specified figure and every pole derived from it moves by ~5x in the wrong direction. (2) *** THE '1 nF MAX CAPACITIVE LOAD' IS AN OPA2197 FIGURE AFTER ALL. *** It is on this part's own p.1 Features ('High Capacitive Load Drive Capability: 1 nF'), in its p.1 Description, and in section 7.3.5 p.22: 'in a unity-gain configuration, directly drives up to 1 nF of pure capacitive load'. The INA828 carries the same headline number by coincidence. The dispute filed against this figure should be closed - and per CLAUDE.md, a correct figure filed as disputed is the dangerous kind, because it stops getting re-checked. Figure 27/28 show 1 nF is a stable-but-ringing limit (~40% overshoot at unity gain), not a 30% threshold; TI recommends a 10-20 ohm isolation resistor and tabulates R_ISO for 45deg/60deg phase margin in Table 3 p.23. CONFIRMED: GBW 10MHz, SR 20V/us, Isc +-65mA, IQ 1mA/amp, ~11.9V swing on +-12V, SOIC-8 DUAL R-thJA 107.9 degC/W (the single OPA197 is 115.8 - different table). NOT-IN-DOCUMENT: the '114 dB PSRR' this corpus cites; TI specifies +-1 uV/V typ and +-3 uV/V max, i.e. 120 dB typ and 110.5 dB worst case. Conclusions unaffected, provenance was not

description: Key chain connector - carrier and cluster boards
notes: DECIDED 2026-09-21. Pinout GND SCK GND SH/LD GND SER GND QH GND 3V3 spare spare - a ground between every signal (ADR 0001 item 1). Raised against ADR 0005; ADR 0005 must widen the spec or the ramp must be programmed by something other than the internal pull-up. Both corners are safe: 537mA of charging at the fast corner still clears the 240mA foldback floor at 0.14V of output and never approaches 940mA

description: Upper leg of the LT1641 FB divider, umbilical +12V to FB
notes: BLOCKING AND NEW 2026-09-21. FB (pin 2) was connected to NOTHING, and foldback tracks V_FB, not V_OUT - so the part held the sense drop at its 12mV floor (240mA) forever, never finished the ramp, and the -1 latched off. Size the divider so V_FB crosses 0.5V EARLY in the ramp, above which the threshold is the full 47mV. FB is also the PWRGD comparator input at 1.233V, so the same divider sets where PWRGD asserts across the ramp. VALUES NOT SET: the foldback law is [web, search-index] and needs 164112fc.pdf | 2026-09-21 VALUE SET, NO LONGER BLOCKING. The foldback law is CONFIRMED VERBATIM against the banked 164112fc.pdf: 'The current limit circuit will regulate the voltage across the sense resistor (VCC - VSENSE) to 47mV when VFB is 0.5V or higher. If VFB drops below 0.5V, the voltage across the sense resistor decreases linearly and stops at 12mV when VFB is 0V' [p.5], drawn as Figure 7 [p.9]. STRUCTURAL POINT THIS ROW DID NOT KNOW: V_FB=0.5V and the PWRGD threshold V_FBH=1.313V are set by the SAME divider, so V_OUT(full 47mV limit) = 0.381 x V_OUT(PWRGD) ALWAYS - 'cross 0.5V early' and 'PWRGD means the output is good' are one decision, not two, and the ratio is fixed by the part. Sized at the PWRGD end because that is the end with a hard requirement: PWRGD must release below the worst-case delivered output of ~11.36V (Eurorack +12V at -5%, less the sense and FET drops). 35.7k/5.11k puts PWRGD at 10.49V nominal (10.05-10.93V over 1% resistors and the 1.280-1.345V V_FBH window) and V_FB=0.5V at 3.99V of output. Divider current 294uA at 12V, i.e. 294x the 1uA max FB input current [p.2], so leakage is <=0.34% of the ratio

description: Straps the DAC8568 LDAC pin to GND
notes: *** CORRECTED 2026-09-21: THIS WAS PULLED TO AVDD AND THAT GATES THE DAC. *** SBAS430E p.38 verbatim: 'For such synchronous updates, the LDAC pin is not required and it must be connected to GND permanently.' description: Isolation resistor, reference buffer dual-feedback network (SBOS737C Fig. 56)
notes: OPA2197 output to SKT-BREATH VS. One of four parts in TI's dual-feedback reference-buffer network; the other three are R-FB-REF, R-FBX-REF and C-FB-REF. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE | 2026-09-21: 10R -> 37.4R, and the justification is replaced rather than amended. SBOS737C section 8.2.3 p.30 Figure 56 'Precision Reference Buffer' is the worked answer for this exact circuit. IT TRANSFERS TO OUR 100 nF DESPITE TI'S 10uF BECAUSE R_ISO IS SET BY Zo, NOT BY C_L - the attenuation R_ISO/(Zo+R_ISO) and the pole-zero ratio both depend only on R_ISO/Zo, and C_L moves both corners together and cancels. 37.4R is Zo/10 against the specified Zo = 375 ohm (p.8). Simulated 85.9 degrees at 896 kHz, and the same model run on Figure 56 as printed returns 87.4 against TI's published 89. DC ERROR ACROSS THIS RESISTOR IS EXACTLY ZERO BY TOPOLOGY - C-FB-REF blocks at DC so no current flows in R-FBX-REF, input current is pA so none flows in R-FB-REF, and the amplifier therefore forces V(VS) = 5.000 V. Its value and tolerance stop mattering; 1% is bought for stock reasons. Power is (10mA)^2 x 37.4 = 3.74 mW in an 0805. THE OLD ROW'S IN-LOOP CHOICE IS REFUTED, NOT SUPERSEDED: in-loop R_ISO buys nothing at ANY value - 1.5 degrees at 10R and 1.5 degrees at 37.4R, the same as fitting nothing. See figures.yaml riso-ref-topology

description: DC feedback resistor, reference buffer - taken at the sensor's VS pin
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | 10k AND NOT TI'S 1M, deliberately. Two reasons TI's circuit does not have. (1) The guaranteed-over-temperature I_B of 5 nA through 1M is 5 mV = 1000 ppm = 3.4 LSB on a rail that IS the ratiometric scale factor; through 10k it is 50 uV = 0.034 LSB. (2) R_F x C_F sets the HANDOVER frequency above which the loop closes on the amplifier's own output instead of on VS. TI's load is a pure capacitor; ours draws 10 mA, so above the handover any load-current change appears at VS across R-ISO-REF. TI's 1M x 39nF puts it at 4.08 Hz, inside the breath channel. 10k x 1nF puts it at 15.9 kHz, well above the 500 Hz channel, and |Z_out| at VS is then 1.20 ohm at 500 Hz. The R-FB-REF:R-FBX-REF RATIO OF 100:1 IS WHAT MUST BE PRESERVED from TI, not the absolute values

description: AC feedback resistor, reference buffer - taken at the OPA2197 output pin
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | Scales with R-FB-REF to hold TI's 100:1 ratio, so that above the handover the loop closes on the amplifier output with only 1% of VS leaking in. R_Fx x C_F is 100 ns here against the 3.74 us TI's own rule (R_Fx C_F = R_ISO C_L) would give, and the simulation says it costs nothing - the binding condition is |R_Fx + 1/(2.pi.f C_F)| much less than R_F AT CROSSOVER, which at 896 kHz is 100 + 178 = 205 ohm against 10k, a 49x margin

description: AC feedback capacitor, reference buffer
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | C0G, because this capacitor sets the handover frequency and an X7R's DC-bias and temperature derating would move it. 1nF at R-FB-REF's 10k gives a 15.9 kHz handover. IT IS ALSO WHY THE DC ERROR IS ZERO: blocking at DC is what leaves R-FB-REF as the only feedback path, so the amplifier servos the SENSOR pin rather than its own output. NOTE FOR THE SPICE DECK: this network leaves the summing node with no DC path except through R-FB-REF, so a simulator needs a leak resistor there for convergence and a real board does not - the amplifier's input leakage provides it

description: Panel breath GAIN - attenuator ahead of the summer
notes: Attenuator, NOT a feedback rheostat - a rheostat makes gain and offset share a resistor and the knobs fight, which is the coupling the REF trimmer was added to remove one stage upstream. 0.125 to 1.000 against a fixed x4 = 0.5 to 4.0 at the jack. WIPER MUST BE BUFFERED: it drives R-IN, so an unbuffered wiper makes the gain depend on a source impedance that varies with rotation. Taper is a feel question and therefore a bench question | 2026-09-21, from the genuine Taiwan Alpha RV09 series datasheet now in the repo (datasheets/connectors/RV09AF-40.pdf). FOUR THINGS THE ORDER CODE HAS TO CARRY, none of which this row said. (1) THE PLAIN -40 HAS NO BUSHING AT ALL - it is snap-in, and the panel needs only shaft clearance. A bushing is a SUFFIX: E1 = metal M9x0.75, E1N = plastic D9, and either makes the panel hole ~9.5mm instead of a shaft hole. (2) CENTRE DETENT IS SUFFIX 0C, and it costs half the life: 5000 rotations with the click against 10000 without. (3) THE A/B LETTER IN RV09A / RV09B IS THE ROTATIONAL ANGLE (280 +/-5 deg vs 300 +/-5 deg), NOT THE TAPER. The taper is a separate A/B/C code. This is a standing trap and the row said nothing about it. (4) Body 9.8mm wide, 11.4mm across the snap-in lugs, 7.0mm board-to-shaft for every -40, shaft D6.0 0/-0.1. THREE ACROSS 50.50mm IS 34.2mm - the pot body is nowhere near binding and the 14mm knob is the constraint, which settles the open question this row carried. NOTE THE PART MAY NOT BE ALPHA: Thonk ships the Song Huei R0904N, dimensionally interchangeable (datasheets/connectors/R0904N.pdf)
